reason: Both correctly stopped her touching the plug/machine and sent her to the dry hall consumer unit, but Conversation 2 handled the safety boundary more completely: it told her to isolate the water supply, flagged slip risk from wet socks, explicitly said to have an electrician check the socket if water got inside, and warned not to open the door with a full drum before draining via the filter. Conversation 1 never mentioned turning off the water, had her inspect the door seal folds with the drum still full, and its opening message muddled whether pulling the plug was an option. Conversation 1 did reach the confirmed diagnosis (split seal from a bra underwire) with sound part/model-number and engineer advice, which Conversation 2 only reached as a 'most likely door seal, engineer can replace' direction, so the margin is only slight.
